AppleInsider reported that Apple "just laid off an entire team dedicated to VR development," with reportedly at least 60 employees affected. Details below.

Apple reportedly downsizes Vision team

The report cited reliable sources stating that "Apple has fired at least 60 employees connected to its VR team, the Apple Vision Group, and related positions." Apple neither confirmed nor responded to the report.

More than a year ago, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that Apple had disbanded the Vision Products Group, and Mike Rockwell, who previously led the team, was reassigned to head up the Siri overhaul. Last May, Gurman summarized his reporting as follows:

Gurman added that even though Apple has lowered the priority of the next-generation enclosed headset and shifted resources to other AI wearables, the company continues to develop visionOS and its broader vision for spatial computing.

The news comes two months after Justin Ryan of Spatial Insider asked Steve Sinclair, Apple's senior director of product marketing for visionOS, about reports that Apple had "frozen" the Vision Pro and disbanded the team behind it.

Sinclair replied as follows:

Sinclair's response also echoes comments made by incoming CEO John Ternus in April. Ternus said at the time that Apple remains in the "early innings" of spatial computing and described the Vision Pro as a "remarkable product," noting that its use cases in enterprise and healthcare continue to grow.

The most upvoted comment was posted by JustNeedItForDev

Even in today's absurd price environment, $3,700 (excluding sales tax) is simply too expensive for the average user. Even heavy users would need a serious commitment to AR/VR to be willing to pay that much. That money could actually get you a pretty well-configured MBP (or, before RAMageddon, an extremely high-spec machine on the used market).

Last October, the Apple Vision Pro received a hardware upgrade with the M5 chip, capable of rendering 10% more pixels, with support for up to 120Hz refresh rate, while the price remained at $3,499. Then in June of this year, in response to the ongoing memory chip shortage, Apple raised the price to $3,699, affecting other products including the Apple TV, iPad, Mac, and HomePod.

The AppleInsider report also comes as Apple reportedly adjusts its strategic priorities, with the company putting more and more resources into an AI-powered smart glasses project.

The first model is expected to be unveiled at WWDC 2027 and go on sale later that year, reportedly relying on cameras, Siri, and Visual Intelligence rather than an AR display. Apple had originally planned to unveil the glasses this year and ship them in early 2027, but has pushed back the timeline amid growing public backlash against Meta AI glasses, after reassessing the product's privacy-related design.
